query_text: Have video referee systems improved sport?

messages.content: Have video referee systems improved sport?

message.content:
**Yes, but only partly.** Video referee systems such as VAR have **improved officiating accuracy** and, in some cases, reduced unfair errors, but they have also introduced **delays, controversy, and a worse fan experience** in some matches and leagues.[1][2][3][4]

In football, the strongest evidence in the results is that VAR was introduced to correct “clear and obvious” errors and improve fairness, and some sources report higher decision accuracy after its adoption.[1][2][4] One source says VAR “clearly improves professional decision making” and “reinstates… fairness and fair play,” while another reports decision accuracy rising from around **92% to over 98%** in major leagues.[1][2]

At the same time, the improvement is not uniform across all types of decisions. A legal analysis notes that VAR has **not eliminated controversial decisions**, especially when calls are subjective rather than factual, and argues that better review standards are still needed.[3] The Wikipedia summary also notes that VAR has been most effective for **offsides and mistaken identity**, while **penalties and disciplinary decisions** remain more contentious.[4]

There is also a tradeoff in match flow and audience enjoyment. Sources note criticisms such as **delays**, **disruptions**, and fans feeling less connected while waiting for decisions, even though one analysis says reviews usually target only game-changing incidents and may not slow matches dramatically overall.[2][3][4]

So the best evidence-supported answer is: **video referee systems have made sports, especially football, more accurate and fair in many situations, but they have not unequivocally “improved” the sport overall because they also create new problems.**
